name: Henry Vassall-Fox, 3rd Baron Holland
credit: Henry Richard Vassall-Fox, 3rd Baron Holland, by Sir George Hayter · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Henry Richard Vassall-Fox, 3rd Baron Holland (1773–1840), was a Whig statesman and nephew of Charles James Fox. Holland House, Kensington, was under him the centre of Whig society and of a famous literary circle; he wrote occasional verse and translations.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: Over a Covered Seat in the Flower-Garden at Holland House
poems.author: Henry Vassall-Fox, 3rd Baron Holland
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
Here Rogers sat, and here for ever dwell.
To me, those pleasures that he sang so well.
